previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with complex bariatric surgical history (prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with later reversal) complicated by chronic abdominal pain and post-prandial hypoglycemia requiring prior dextrose infusions via PICC, and a seizure disorder on levetiracetam, was admitted after a witnessed ~3-minute seizure with fever, leukocytosis, elevated lactate, and fluid-responsive hypotension concerning for sepsis. Imaging showed left lower lobe pneumonia and no acute intra-abdominal process. Blood cultures grew coagulase-negative Staphylococcus (Staph epidermidis) in one bottle, raising concern for central-line associated bloodstream infection; the PICC was removed (tip culture without significant growth), Infectious Diseases recommended a 7-day course of IV vancomycin, repeat surveillance cultures remained negative, and transthoracic echocardiogram showed no valvular vegetations. Neurology increased levetiracetam to 1000 mg twice daily. Endocrinology and Nutrition evaluated hypoglycemia and malnutrition risk, attributing symptoms to post-prandial hypoglycemia exacerbated by high-glycemic foods; diet was advanced to a diabetic/consistent-carbohydrate plan with small frequent meals and Glucerna supplementation, and glucose remained stable without ongoing D5 infusions despite intermittent severe abdominal pain requiring breakthrough hydromorphone. She was discharged home hemodynamically stable, tolerating small meals, with close neurology and endocrinology/nutrition follow-up and bowel regimen and opioid safety planning.

BRIEF SUMMARY 
==============

___ is a ___ year old women with a history of RYGB 
surgery in ___ s/p reversal in ___. She had numerous 
complications including marginal ulcers, chronic epigastric pain 
s/p LOA earlier in ___ without resolution of pain, 
gastroparesis confirmed by GES, and post-gastric bypass 
hypoglycemia previously receiving J tube feeds. She has been 
hospitalized at ___ 67 times since ___. She also has PTSD, 
anxiety, and depression, and is currently on disability for 
seizures which are fairly well controlled with Keppra. Of note, 
this is her ___ admission since being admitted for weight loss 
surgery in ___.  

Patient was in her usual state of health (which consists of a 
constant epigastric pain, anywhere from ___ episodes of 
vomiting per day, and ___ small volume liquid stools with 
abdominal cramping) until ___ days ago when she noticed the 
epigastric pain began to radiate around the right side of her 
abdomen towards her back. Her J tube was in her abdominal wall 
and removed in ED, but her pain continued. A RUQ u/s and CT A/P 
and LFTs did not show any other cause for her pain. She was 
evaluated by the surgery team, who felt that there were no 
surgical interventions indicated at the time. She also had 
episodes of hypoglycemia and blood pressures in the ___, which 
were felt to be from poor PO intake and treated with IV fluids. 
She was noted to have several nutritional deficiencies, and was 
followed by nutrition. Ultimately it was decided that given that 
her primary surgeon is at ___, transfer to ___ 
would be beneficial in further management.

=========================
PROBLEM-BASED SUMMARY 
=========================

#Abdominal pain
Patient presented with a new acute abdominal pain around the 
right upper quadrant, wrapping around to her back, which is new 
from her chronic pain. She was evaluated in the ED with a CT 
abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast and abdominal ultrasound. The CT 
showed a malpositioned J tube (previously known) and otherwise 
no findings to show cause of pain. The J tube was removed 
without incident by the surgery team in the ED. However, the 
patient's pain persisted, and so she was admitted to the 
medicine service. The patient's pain had been managed with IV 
morphine in the ED, which only made her nauseous. She was 
started on oxycodone on the floor, which did help her pain. 
However, she continued to be in pain, and was unable to tolerate 
significant POs. She became somewhat hypotensive to the ___, 
and intermittently required fluids while in the hospital. She 
was also mildly hypoglycemic to the ___, also treated with IVF. 
A review of outpatient labs revealed nutritional deficiencies. 
She was started on vit D in the hospital. Given her persisting 
symptoms, it was felt that the patient would best be served by 
transfer to ___, where further discussions could be had with 
her surgeon. 

#Poor PO intake
#Concern for malnutrition
We discussed at length the difficulty of coming up with a 
nutrition plan given that too much food by mouth causes pain and 
vomiting given the gastroparesis, J tube has already become 
misplaced and is likely risky to re-place given her numerous 
abdominal procedures, and nutrition via an IV is a high 
infection risk. The nutrition team spoke with her for diet 
education as they have on prior admissions. 

#Vitamin D deficiency 
Started on 50,000 oral weekly repletion 

#Iron deficiency 
Would consider IV iron infusion as outpatient 

Chronic issues:

#Epigastric pain 
Was continued on her home pain regimen. Plan for pain management 
follow up with Dr. ___ ___.

#Post Gastric Bypass Hypoglycemia 
As above, patient occasionally found to be hypoglycemic with low 
of 70, likely due to poor PO intake. Was monitored with Q6H 
fingersticks, and received D5 IVF. 

#Gastroparesis 
#Chronic nausea and vomiting 
Continued home metoclopramide 10 mg PO TID w/ meals, 
Prochlorperazine 10 mg PO TID:PRN nausea, Ondansetron ODT 4 mg 
PO Q8H:PRN nausea, LORazepam 1 mg PO TID:PRN anxiety and nausea, 
Gastric pacer being discussed with outpatient surgeon 

#History of marginal ulcer

DAILY 

#Seizure
Continued home Levetiracetam 1000 mg PO Q12H

#Insomnia 
#Anxiety 
#Depression 
#PTSD

=================================
TRANSITIONAL ISSUES
=================================

- Patient was noted to have previous labs from outpatient 
setting showing several nutritional deficiencies, including iron 
and vitamin D. She was started on vitamin D in the hospital. It 
is unclear that she will be able to meet her nutritional needs 
with PO intake alone. 
- Pressures at times remained somewhat soft, (90s/___), and 
responded with IVF. Felt to be secondary to poor PO intake. 
- Blood glucose levels at times borderline low in the ___, 
likely from poor PO intake. Should be closely monitored, but 
patient has good hypoglycemic awareness. 
- Pain control remained challenging, had some improvement with 
small doses of PO oxycodone. Would try to wean as tolerated. 
- Gtube removed during this admission given malposition seen on 
CT a/p.
- EKG should be monitored for QTC prolongation
- Patient received oxycodone 10mg Q4h prn severe pain for

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector CT images of the abdomen and pelvis were acquired
without intravenous contrast. Non-contrast scan has several limitations in
detecting vascular and parenchymal organ abnormalities, including tumor
detection.
Oral contrast was administered.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

DOSE:  Total DLP (Body) = 808 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CT of the abomen and pelvis from ___.

FINDINGS: 

LOWER CHEST: Visualized lung fields are within normal limits.  There is no
evidence of pleural or pericardial effusion.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: The liver demonstrates homogeneous attenuation throughout. 
There is no evidence of focal lesions within the limitations of an unenhanced
scan.  There is no evidence of intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary
dilatation.  The gallbladder is within normal limits.

PANCREAS: The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions within the limitations of an unenhanced scan.  There is no
pancreatic ductal dilatation.  There is no peripancreatic stranding.

SPLEEN: The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesions.

ADRENALS: The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY: The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size.  There is no evidence
of focal renal lesions within the limitations of an unenhanced scan.  There is
no hydronephrosis.  There is no nephrolithiasis.  There is no perinephric
abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL: Gastrostomy tube is malpositioned, terminating in the
anterior abdominal wall.  Post Roux-en-Y gastric bypass reversal.  Small bowel
loops demonstrate normal caliber and wall thickness throughout.  The colon and
rectum are within normal limits.  The appendix is not visualized but there are
no secondary signs of appendicitis.

PELVIS: The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  There is no
free fluid in the pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS: The uterus and bilateral adnexae are within normal
limits.

LYMPH NODES: There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR: There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  No atherosclerotic disease
is noted.

BONES: There is no evidence of worrisome osseous lesions or acute fracture.

SOFT TISSUES: Gastrostomy tube is malpositioned, terminating in the anterior
abdominal wall without adjacent fluid collection.

IMPRESSION:


1. Malpositioned gastrostomy tube, terminating in the anterior abdominal wall.
No adjacent collection.
2. Post Roux-en-Y gastric bypass reversal without evidence of obstruction or
pneumoperitoneum.
